result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B covers more of what the rubric asks for. It adds loading, empty and error states with a real Try again button. Its Download is a real link with an aria-label naming the month, and it fixes the 44px tap target. A raises useful extra points: XSS, server-side authorization and CSP. But its error state only says to refresh with no retry control, its buttons all read "Download" with no month, and neither answer adds an explicit focus style or right-aligns or formats the totals. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep the working fetch and the download endpoint, fix the innerHTML injection, and add loading, empty and error states. A goes further: it adds a Try again button and turns Download into a real link whose accessible name includes the month. B's error message offers no retry, and its Download buttons are focusable but all have the same name. Neither answer mentions visible focus styling or lines the totals up, and B adds some useful but generic server-side and CSP checks.
